content: Prior resolved seed ticket: 7020. This knowledge is intentionally from a different ticket than active demo ticket 7001, but its wording should match ticket 7001 symptoms: Status API unavailable; Customer reports API is down; Ubuntu status API localhost:8080/health unavailable after reboot; service worked after manual restart; systemd service not enabled; wrong unit name suspected; no listener on TCP port 8080 after reboot; customer storefront or nginx proxy can show 502 Bad Gateway because the upstream status API is absent. Customer: Nordlicht Logistik GmbH / Example GmbH demo customer. Priority: high. Final status: DONE. Customer benefit to restore: stable HTTP 200 from http://localhost:8080/health and the customer-facing status page after reboot. Seed scope: simulated completed workflow for local demo and retrieval only; it does not describe a hidden evaluation incident.

Context and root cause for prior ticket 7020, which should help active ticket 7001 style symptoms: the Ubuntu VM was reachable over SSH, but nothing listened on localhost port 8080 after reboot and curl to http://localhost:8080/health failed. systemctl --failed listed no failed units because the status API was not being started at boot. Manual service start made the health endpoint work briefly, which pointed away from nginx and network failure and toward startup persistence. The technical cause was that the status API systemd unit was disabled or the app was registered under a different unit name than the technician first checked. The durable diagnosis is: locate the actual status API unit, confirm it starts the process bound to port 8080, then enable that exact unit so reboot starts the API automatically. Simulated audit trail: run_created for ticket 7020; customer_system_loaded with redacted host details; ssh_access_confirmed_by_technician; action_proposed for listener check on port 8080; action_approved; command_completed exit 0 with no listener; action_proposed for failed units; action_approved; command_completed exit 0 with none failed; action_proposed for systemd unit discovery; action_approved; command_completed exit 0; action_proposed for targeted enable and restart of the identified status API unit; action_approved with write classification; command_completed exit 0; validation_requested; validation_confirmed_by_technician; activity_reviewed; activity_submitted; phoenix_ticket_status_patched_DONE.

Sanitized command snippets and responses from the completed workflow for Status API unavailable / API is down / localhost:8080/health unavailable after reboot / service worked after manual restart / systemd service not enabled / wrong unit name. 1) Command: ss -ltnp sport = :8080. Classification: read_only. Approved: yes. Exit: 0. Response snippet: no listener on port 8080 after reboot. 2) Command: systemctl --failed --no-pager. Classification: read_only. Approved: yes. Exit: 0. Response snippet: 0 loaded units listed, so the outage was not visible as a failed service. 3) Command: systemctl list-unit-files --type=service --no-pager | grep -Ei 'status|api'. Classification: read_only. Approved: yes. Exit: 0. Response snippet: identified the actual status API service unit and whether it was disabled; no secret output included. 4) Command: systemctl --no-pager status status-api.service. Classification: read_only. Approved: yes. Exit: 3. Response snippet: first guessed unit was inactive, disabled, or not found, indicating possible wrong unit name. 5) Command: systemctl --no-pager status phoenix-status-api.service. Classification: read_only. Approved: yes. Exit: 3. Response snippet: actual unit existed but was disabled or inactive after boot. 6) Command: sudo -n systemctl enable --now phoenix-status-api.service. Classification: write_targeted. Approved: yes. Exit: 0. Response snippet: created boot-start symlink and started only the identified status API service. 7) Command: systemctl is-enabled phoenix-status-api.service. Classification: read_only. Approved: yes. Exit: 0. Response snippet: enabled. 8) Command: curl --max-time 5 -fsS -o /dev/null -w 'http_status=%{http_code}' http://localhost:8080/health. Classification: read_only. Approved: yes. Exit: 0. Response snippet: http_status=200. Commands summary intentionally omits environment values, tokens, raw logs, and secret output.

Actions taken in order for prior ticket 7020: confirmed SSH access only after technician approval; verified that no process listened on TCP port 8080 after reboot; checked failed units and found none, which explained why systemctl --failed did not identify the root cause; searched systemd service names related to status and API; compared the guessed unit name with the actual status API unit; confirmed the actual unit was disabled or inactive; enabled and started only the identified status API service with systemctl enable --now; left nginx, firewall, databases, logs, and unrelated filesystem paths unchanged. Activity summary: restored the status API by enabling the correct systemd service unit so the application starts on boot and binds localhost:8080. Root cause: the status API service was not enabled under the actual systemd unit name, so after reboot nothing listened on port 8080 even though manual start could make the API work. Commands summary: listener, systemd status, unit discovery, targeted enable/start, and HTTP health validation; no secrets or raw sensitive output included.

Validation result for prior ticket 7020: systemctl is-active for the identified status API unit returned active, systemctl is-enabled returned enabled, ss showed a listener on localhost:8080, and curl --max-time 5 -fsS http://localhost:8080/health returned HTTP 200 with a sanitized healthy response. A repeat request through the customer-facing proxy returned HTTP 200 instead of 502 Bad Gateway, proving the customer-facing status API was restored. Persistence check: because the actual unit is enabled, the fix survives reboot and does not rely on a manual restart. Completed Phoenix activity payload fields: ticket_id=7020; start_datetime=2026-06-07T10:00:00Z; end_datetime=2026-06-07T10:18:00Z; summary=Restored the customer-facing status API by enabling and starting the correct systemd service unit; root_cause=The status API service was not enabled under the actual unit name, so it did not start after reboot and nothing listened on localhost:8080; actions_taken=Diagnosed missing listener, checked failed units, discovered the actual service unit, enabled and started that unit, validated HTTP 200; commands_summary=ss, systemctl, bounded curl checks, and one targeted systemctl enable/start with secret-bearing output omitted; validation_result=status API unit active and enabled, localhost:8080 health endpoint returned HTTP 200, and the customer-facing endpoint no longer returned 502. Final workflow state: activity submitted successfully and ticket status patched to DONE.
